title: Bash vs PowerShell Side by Side
oneLiner: The same everyday tasks in both shells, searchable, plus the differences in philosophy that trip people up.
keyTakeaway: bash passes text and you pick fields by position; PowerShell passes objects and you pick properties by name. Most tasks map one to one: grep is Select-String, tail -f is Get-Content -Wait, systemctl is Get-Service and friends, ssh host cmd is Invoke-Command. Watch for case sensitivity, $? and comparison operators.
explanation: Most IT jobs mix Linux and Windows, so you'll switch between bash and PowerShell constantly. This lesson is a phrasebook: a searchable table of everyday tasks in both shells, the differences in how they think, and one real task solved both ways.
